claims.text: High configurational entropy in single-phase CrFeCoNiX produces a random, homogeneous distribution of Cr, Fe, Co, Ni, and X.
High configurational entropy produces a defect-minimized CrFeCoNiX alloy microstructure.
Exposure of single-phase CrFeCoNiX above 900 °C promotes formation of a stable, coherent, slow-growing protective oxide layer.
Uniformly distributed alloying elements drive formation of a continuous oxide scale.
The single-phase, high-entropy state suppresses rapid and heterogeneous diffusion during oxidation.
Suppressing rapid and heterogeneous diffusion minimizes internal stress in the oxide scale.
Multiphase CrFeCoNiX alloys have less uniform or segregated cation distributions.
Compositional inhomogeneity in multiphase alloys causes uneven or heterogeneous oxide growth.
Uneven oxide growth creates local stress concentrations.
Local stress concentrations cause cracking or spallation of the oxide scale.
Under identical exposures, single-phase CrFeCoNiX will form more coherent, homogeneous, and slowly growing oxide scales than multiphase CrFeCoNiX.
Multiphase CrFeCoNiX will be more likely than single-phase CrFeCoNiX to develop cracked or spalled oxide scales.
Configurational entropy can drive a reversible transformation from a multiphase oxide to a single-phase oxide.
The entropy-stabilized single-phase oxide reported in the cited evidence has random and homogeneous cation distributions.
The proposed behavior is limited to CrFeCoNiX alloys above 900 °C in oxygen-rich or corrosive atmospheres.
Different temperatures, atmosphere compositions, or alloy configurations may produce different oxide behavior.
Failure of the single-phase alloy to outperform the multiphase control in oxide coherence, homogeneity, growth rate, or stress behavior would falsify the hypothesis.
